analysis: The code snippet calls `Iterator.next()` on the iterator obtained from `abilities.values().iterator()` in multiple places. The only declared exception is `NoSuchElementException`, thrown when the iteration has no more elements. The first call occurs inside an `if` condition that checks `abilities.size() == 1`, ensuring the iterator has at least one element. The second call (line 4) is inside the same conditional block, so also safe. The third call (line 12) occurs inside a separate `if` block that only checks `userData.isUseFirstManaAbility()`, `object instanceof Permanent`, and land card type, but does **not** verify that `abilities` is non-empty. If `abilities` is empty at that point, `next()` will throw `NoSuchElementException`. No other checks or validations prevent this exception at that call site.
answer: NoSuchElementException is not fully avoided because the call at line 12 (inside the second if block) can be executed when `abilities` is empty, which would cause the exception. All other calls to `next()` are guarded by a size check.
remark: The `NoSuchElementException` can be triggered if the `abilities` map is empty when the second if condition (line 10-14) is entered. Specifically, if `userData.isUseFirstManaAbility()` is true, `object` is a `Permanent`, and its card type contains `LAND`, then `abilities.values().iterator().next()` is called without verifying that `abilities` contains any elements. This scenario can occur when `activateAbility` is invoked with an empty map, causing the iterator to have no next element.
